test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: We express the concentration of solution in various ways. Which of the following method is INCORRECT?

options.text: Volume by volume percentage of a solution
Mass by mass percentage of a solution
Volume by mass percentage of a solution
Mass by volume percentage of a solution

solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume by mass percentage of a solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **concentration of a solution** is the amount of **solute** present in a given amount (**mass or volume**) of solution, or the amount of solute dissolved in a given mass or volume of **solvent**.
 
• **Mass by mass percentage** of a solution is calculated as the (**Mass of solute** / **Mass of solution**) × **100**. This is a common and correct method for expressing concentration, especially when dealing with two solid components. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Mass by volume percentage** of a solution is calculated as the (**Mass of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**. This method is widely used in **medicine** and **pharmacy**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Volume by volume percentage** of a solution is calculated as the (**Volume of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**. This is used when both the solute and the solvent are **liquids**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Volume by mass percentage** is not a standard or scientifically recognized method for expressing the concentration of a solution in general chemistry, as **volume** changes with **temperature** while **mass** remains constant, making this ratio inconsistent. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solute and Solvent**: In a **homogeneous mixture**, the component present in a **smaller quantity** is the **solute**, while the component present in the **larger quantity** is the **solvent**.
 
• **Molarity (M)**: It is defined as the number of **moles** of solute dissolved in **one litre** of solution. It is one of the most commonly used units of concentration in **laboratories**.
 
• **Molality (m)**: This is the number of **moles** of solute per **kilogram** (**kg**) of the **solvent**. Unlike molarity, molality does not change with **temperature**.
 
• **Saturated Solution**: A solution in which **no more solute** can be dissolved at a particular **temperature** is called a **saturated solution**. The amount of solute present in it at this temperature is called its **solubility**.
 
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: When a solute is present in **trace quantities**, the concentration is expressed in **ppm**. It is calculated as (**Number of parts of the component** / **Total number of parts of all components of the solution**) × **10⁶**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Dependence**: Concentration terms like **Molarity**, **Volume percentage**, and **Mass by Volume percentage** change with **temperature** because **volume** is dependent on temperature.
 
• **Temperature Independence**: Concentration terms like **Mass percentage**, **Molality**, and **Mole fraction** are **independent** of temperature because they are based on **mass**.
 
• **Mole Fraction**: It is the **ratio** of the number of moles of a particular component to the **total number of moles** of all the components in the solution. The sum of all mole fractions in a solution is always **equal to one**.
